label: If y has POWER_OVER_ESSE_1 over x, x can fail to be in substance or y is a CAUSE_2 of x's esse
paraphrase: OPEN (correlation), analyst formulation, attribution deferred (navigation: Met. Theta.1 1046a, active power correlates with passive potency; ST I q.104 a.3, annihilation as ceasing to give being, not an action on a patient): for all y and x, if y has power over x's esse in the broad sense (POWER_OVER_ESSE_1: a power to make or unmake x's being), then x can fail to be in substance (POSSIBLE_NOT_TO_BE_1, the in-subject channel) or y is a CAUSE_2 of x's esse. A co-occurrence disjunction: it does not state that the power works on x's potency or that it is the giving of esse; the Aristotelian rationale is that it does one or the other. CausesIn is tenseless, so a cause that conserves x and a cause that only originated x are not distinguished: a deist originator satisfies this premise; only a tensed (conserving) strengthening would exclude it. Under the narrower giving sense POWER_OVER_ESSE_2 the premise is trivial (controls, law 11), so the batch uses the broad sense. Its omission model is an inert power-holder (controls, inertPowerHolder).
